patch.dateConfidenceReasoning: The Australian Prime Minister’s official opening speech is dated 25 October 2026 and marks the airport’s opening. This verifies the opening date rather than relying on the earlier schedule.
patch.longFormSummary:
Opening verified — October 30, 2026

The Australian Government held the official opening of Western Sydney International Airport on October 25, 2026. Its opening speech confirms the airport’s 3.7 km runway and AUD 5.3 billion government investment.

Earlier announcement and project evidence

  • Western Sydney International (Nancy-Bird Walton) Airport, WSI, at Luddenham and Badgerys Creek, is opening for passengers on 25 October 2026, after cargo flights began on 27 July 2026
  • It is a full-service, curfew-free airport for up to 10 million passengers a year with a single 3.7 km runway, after 15 years of planning, seven of construction and a year of testing
  • Jetstar operates the first commercial flight (A320 to the Gold Coast, 11am 25 October), with Melbourne and Brisbane routes; Air New Zealand to Auckland from 26 October; Singapore Airlines daily from 23 November 2026; QantasLink from 28 March 2027
  • From 1 November 2026 WSI is intended to take overnight freight movements under the Sydney Airport Curfew Act 1995
  • The project created over 12,800 jobs and is part of nearly $18 billion of Western Sydney investment; terminal completed 11 June 2025 and the first jet landed 28 October 2025

pinContentCorrections.reason: Verify the realized airport opening instead of leaving it classified as a future scheduled event.

patch.description: Freebird DC01 is the filed 548,950 sq ft, four-data-hall first building at SB Energy’s Milam County data center in Burlington, Texas. Its TDLR filing estimates USD 470 million and lists October 15, 2026 as a completion target. That target is unconfirmed; the developer currently reports Phase 1 construction and expects first operations in 2027.
patch.dateConfidenceReasoning: October 15, 2026 is retained as the original TDLR-filed building completion target, not an achieved handover. The developer currently says Phase 1 is in construction and first operations are expected in 2027; no DC01-specific actual completion day is published.
patch.longFormSummary:
Current stage checked — October 30, 2026

The developer’s current project FAQ states: Phase 1 of the project is in construction. First operations are expected in 2027. The October 15, 2026 TDLR target remains unconfirmed and must not be read as completed construction. Campus-level power or workforce figures are not attributed to this individual DC01 building.

Original Phase 1 filing and earlier research

  • A Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation filing (TABS2026017746, registered 15 April 2026) for Freebird Data Center Phase 1 (DC01) gives a start date of 20 October 2025 and a completion date of 15 October 2026
  • The project is new construction on County Road 133 in Burlington, Milam County, Texas, with an estimated cost of $470 million, privately funded on private land
  • The scope is a single-story 548,950 sq ft data center with four data halls, supporting infrastructure, a loading dock and administrative offices
  • The owner of record is Milam County Data Center LLC, the tenant contact is Kaylen Bushell of OpenAI, and the design firm is Corgan Architects
  • The site is a 1.2 GW facility that SB Energy, a SoftBank subsidiary, is building and operating, led by Zoheir Taheri, with OpenAI also an investor in SB Energy
  • The data center is expected to grow larger in later phases
  • The dates are proposed schedule dates and do not confirm construction progress; the filing's status is 'Project Registered', with plan review pending
  • The filing does not name the general contractor or other trade contractors
  • Datacentermap lists the site as under construction

pinContentCorrections.reason: Distinguish the original filed completion target from current developer evidence; no completion inferred from an elapsed date.
